description: EPIC. A first-class callable value is a closure (code pointer + captures-in-self). How it is CALLED must follow its calling convention (a property of its surface/type), not how many static identities it has. Today the compiler has exactly two bins: a single static closure_lit -> direct typed call; ANYTHING else -> the uniform all-ValueRef boxed seam. The entire typed-but-multi-identity middle (a phi of same-signature function references) is wrongly dumped into the boxed bin, forcing heap boxing of args and returns that a typed indirect call would not need. Witness: fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_value_join.fz and fixtures2/00231 (reducer = case ... -> add_a; _ -> add_b, passed to Enum.reduce). Goal: representation follows convention, uniformly, the same way a scalar is RawInt unless a consumer erases its type to ValueRef. A first-class callable with a concrete uniform surface is dispatched by a typed call_indirect through its body entry; only a surfaceless/opaque callable is boxed. Correct-by-construction; no shims/adapters; rip out the boxed_first_class blanket.
title: First-class callables dispatch by calling convention, not identity count
